_readme: Normaliser test spec — the build hangs off this file.
Each case: raw ASR-style text in, structured transaction out.
Amounts are integers in the currency's minor-free unit (NGN, KES).
Rule: deterministic grammar first, LLM fallback only when grammar returns null.
PROVENANCE: tier-a (pcm-yo-NG) utterances were drafted by an AI assistant and
CORRECTED by a native Nigerian Pidgin/Yoruba speaker (David) before recording.
sw-KE and ha-NG cases remain non-native drafts pending venue validation (flagged per-case).
Even this test corpus required native-speaker repair — the same gap the product exists to close.

packs.pcm-yo-NG: Nigerian Pidgin / Yoruba / English mix, NGN

cases.utterance: I don sell three derica of rice five thousand five
cases.note: native-corrected: 'five thousand five' = 5500 ('five k five' was AI-Pidgin)

cases.utterance: sell one bag of beans forty five k
I buy fuel ten thousand naira
customer take two paint rubber of garri two two fifty
cases.note: NATIVE CORRECTION: reduplicated money is the distributive — 'two two fifty' = 250 each, unambiguously. An outsider (and the AI that drafted this corpus) hears ambiguity; native grammar encodes the distributive. Formerly expected clarify.

cases.utterance: sell garri egberun meta
oya log am one congo of crayfish egbeje o din owo
cases.note: Deliberately hard Yoruba money phrase. If grammar can't parse confidently -> clarify, never silently guess.

cases.utterance: two mudu of elubo one five each
cases.note: NATIVE-VALIDATED as-is: 'one five each' = 1500 each is real usage

cases.utterance: abeg how much I don make today
wetin I sell pass this week
no no na five k not five thousand five
cases.note: native-corrected money phrasing; correction pattern unchanged

cases.utterance: that one na credit she go pay on Friday
cases.note: credit sale flag on last entry — traders sell on credit constantly, judges from this world will notice

cases.utterance: close the day give me summary
sell pure water two bag one two
cases.note: NATIVE-VALIDATED as-is: 'one two' = 1200; 'pure water' survives as one item

cases.utterance: nimeuza mahindi gunia mbili elfu tatu
cases.note: VALIDATE WITH NATIVE SPEAKER. Intended: sold maize, two sacks, 3000

cases.utterance: nimenunua mafuta mia tano
cases.note: VALIDATE. Intended: bought cooking oil/fuel 500 — 'mafuta' ambiguity is itself a good test

cases.utterance: leo nimepata pesa ngapi
cases.note: VALIDATE. Intended: how much have I made today

cases.utterance: sold sukari one kilo mia moja hamsini
na sayar da shinkafa buhu daya dubu talatin
cases.note: VALIDATE WITH NATIVE SPEAKER. Intended: sold rice, one sack, 30000

cases.utterance: nawa na samu yau
cases.note: VALIDATE. Intended: how much did I make today

cases.utterance: log am make I hear
cases.note: No transaction content at all. Agent must ask what to log, not hallucinate an entry. Guard against the LLM fallback inventing data.

cases.utterance: I don sell garri finish
cases.note: native-drafted clarify showcase: completed sale, NO amount spoken. Agent must ask (market-natural: 'How much you sell the garri?') and MUST NOT log until the amount arrives.

acceptance_rules: A case passes only on exact structural match of 'expect' (ignore field order).
Grammar-first: cases 1-5, 7-13, 21 must pass WITHOUT the LLM fallback.
Cases 6, 20, 21 must return clarify — a confident wrong parse on these is a FAIL worse than a crash.
Case 4 must parse the reduplication-distributive CONFIDENTLY (native-speaker validated).
Never fabricate an amount. Null + clarify beats a guess, always.
New language pack = new config file + new cases here. No normaliser code changes allowed.
